phase: Issue #154 Phase 2-C2.5-D2-a: Node memory effect of the Ideal-only Planner Alternative publication (post-hoc analysis)

environment.runtime: Node (Vite SSR loader, one fresh child process per Search run, NOT a Browser Worker)

conditions.memoryValues: process.memoryUsage() periodic samples are sampled maxima, never a true peak; v8FatalGc is V8's own trace line at an OOM death

workloadSelection.rule: OOM representatives: every C2.5-A evidence context with role oom_representative, classification search_only_oom_reproduced and out_of_memory in both C2.5-A modes. Controls: in the C2.5-A evidence contexts order (its selection order, then work index), the first completed_control context ending first_candidate in both modes and the first ending stopped_by_extent_before_candidate in both modes. No Target, Entry or orientation ID is fixed in source.

formalConclusions: Search semantics: both completed controls (c8-p1#0 first_candidate, c13-p4#0 stopped_by_extent_before_candidate) reproduce the C2.5-A status, Search summary, first Candidate key SHA-256, extent / exhausted flags and, in the instrumented mode, the exact prediction counts. Minimal and instrumented agree on every context that ended normally.

Outcome B (partial): of the three C2.5-A Search-only OOM representatives, one left the out-of-memory ending in both modes. c0-p0#0 (deep type) now ends stopped_by_extent_before_candidate (Gogma max depth 233 of the 235 extent, no Candidate), sampled max heapUsed 4.47 GB instrumented / 4.50 GB minimal. c12-p0#0 and c2-p1#0 (shallow type) are still out_of_memory in both modes.
c0-p0#0 reaching the extent is not 'memory issue solved': it delivers no Candidate within the Production default extent, and its Search still used ~4.5 GB of sampled heap.

The retained memory per generated Gogma state dropped: descriptive heapUsed delta per cumulative generated state (last snapshot minus pre-Search) ~9.1 kB -> ~1.8 kB (c0-p0), ~1.8 kB -> ~0.39 kB (c12-p0), ~1.9 kB -> ~0.40 kB (c2-p1). This is a correlation-level descriptive ratio, not an allocation attribution.

The shallow OOM contexts progress about four times further before dying: cumulative generated Gogma states 4.27 M -> 17.40 M (c12-p0) and 4.31 M -> 17.27 M (c2-p1), Gogma max depth 5 -> 12 and 7 -> 18, wall time to the OOM 76 s -> 91 s and 67 s -> 101 s (minimal).

Completed controls use far less memory and time: sampled max heapUsed 3.67 GB -> 0.60 GB (c8-p1 instrumented), 2.26 GB -> 0.40 GB (c13-p4 instrumented); maxRSS 3.81 GB -> 0.78 GB and 2.44 GB -> 0.62 GB (minimal); time to the first Candidate 10.5 s -> 4.6 s (c8-p1 minimal).
notYetClaimable: That the Planner Alternative kernel no longer OOMs for this Export: only the Search-only first-Candidate run of 5 contexts was measured, and two representatives still OOM.
Any Browser (Chrome Dedicated Worker) effect: D2-b.
A true peak heap: all process.memoryUsage() values are sampled maxima; OOM before values are the C2.5-A last snapshot.

Which remaining structure holds the heap of the shallow OOMs after D2-a: no heap snapshot or profile was taken in D2-a; the remaining-structure list is carried over from C2.5-C / D1 and not re-measured.
That c0-p0#0 would deliver a Candidate with a wider extent, or that a Candidate exists at all for it.

directlyRemovedForNonIdealPositions: Route operation arrays (bonusAmendmentOperations(): steps.slice + one RouteOperation per own amendment; resetSkillsOperations())
evaluated objects and their semantic key strings (bonusKey, retentionKey, operationTypeKey, semanticKey), materialQuantity
sort inputs and the {...evaluated, index} copies
channel.retained entries (Planner Alternative channel.retained now holds Ideal positions only)
remaining: held-aware stream raw states in bonusStream set.depths (every generated state of every depth, kept for the stream's lifetime)
raw steps[] arrays per raw solution (length = depth, pointers to shared step objects)
the result node chain (BonusAmendmentResultNode) per state
the per-depth generated array during generation (the single-depth burst: 1.96 M states at depth 3 in c12-p0, 1.26 M in c2-p1)
prediction memos (Reset per position, Keep per family layout and position)
temporary allocations of satisfiesIdealBonuses() for every raw solution

limitations: Node (Vite SSR loader) fresh child processes, 8192 MB heap, jit_default, one machine; not a Browser Worker.
Workload: 3 OOM representatives and 2 completed controls selected from the C2.5-A evidence by the C2.5-C rule; not every orientation or Target of the Export.
C2.5-A minimal mode sampled no memory, so minimal before values exist only as V8's fatal GC line (OOM) or maxRSS / post-Search memory (completed).
The minimal mode of this Phase samples memory every 2 s outside the Search plus the pre / post-Search samples; short runs have few samples.

OOM after values are the last sample received before the death and V8's fatal GC line; the committed heap reached the limit (~8.26 GB committed) while V8 reported ~6.8 GB used at the fatal Mark-Compact.
One run per (context, mode); no repetition statistics.

nextPhaseRecommendation.proceedToD2b: Yes: Search semantics are unchanged and the Node effect is substantial (one representative left OOM, the others progress ~4x further, controls use ~1/6 of the heap). D2-b should re-measure the same contexts in a Chrome Dedicated Worker, expecting the shallow representatives to remain out of memory there.
nextMemoryCandidates: Shallow type (c12-p0, c2-p1 still OOM): the held-aware stream's own raw state storage. set.depths keeps every generated raw state (bonuses, steps[], result node) for the stream's lifetime although each depth is read once per channel; and a single depth generates up to ~2 M states before the frontier reduction. Candidates: release a depth from set.depths once every subscribing channel has read it, derive steps from the result node chain on demand, and bound the per-depth generation working set. These are stream-side changes and need their own semantic audit (late subscribers / replay) like D1.
Deep type (c0-p0 left OOM but still ~4.5 GB): the same set.depths / steps[] retention grows with cumulative states x depth; the same stream-side candidate applies.
Before choosing, a C2.5-C style heap snapshot of the post-D2-a shallow OOM would confirm which of these holds the remaining heap.
